candidates.statement: The individualized therapies discussed in this guidance are limited to diseases that have a well- 108 characterized, identifiable molecular or cellular abnormality, and the therapeutic product targets 109 the underlying abnormality, its proximal pathogenic pathway, or a well-characterized 110 downstream or compensatory mechanism with a clear mechanistic rationale. Nonclinical data 111 that support sufficient editing or target engagement are needed to justify initiation of treatment in 112 humans and may also provide confirmatory evidence. 13 In patients for whom the natural history 113 of the disease in the untreated state can be reasonably characterized, it may be possible for an 114 externally controlled clinical investigation that assesses a patient’s change following treatment 115 compared to baseline to serve as the adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation 116 necessary to support approval/licensure. A substantial improvement in symptoms or change in 117 disease trajectory that is inconsistent with the natural history of the disease may provide 118 substantial evidence of effectiveness. The data submitted by the sponsor must adequately 119 demonstrate that the improvement in outcome cannot reasonably be attributed to alternative 120 treatments or natural variability in the disease phenotype. 121

candidates.statement: For sponsors who intend to submit a marketing application for an individualized therapy, 123 planning for evidence generation to support the efficacy and safety of the product should ideally 124 begin as soon as the patient and genetic target are identified. Given the inherent limitations in 125 the size of clinical development programs, early planning will allow more robust collection of 126 data from various sources, which have the potential to be leveraged as evidence to support a 127 future marketing application. Planning should also include establishing the appropriate 128 chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) needed to support the generation of safety and 129 efficacy data and subsequently, product approval/licensure. 130
